findings.description: The plan allows journey.consumer=both, but F002's required_evidence_classes API is defined over a single consumer value and only pins invalid-tuple behavior for human and agent. It does not state whether consumer=both is accepted per surface, rewritten into the surface's pinned family, or rejected at the pure-function boundary.
findings.recommendation: Pin consumer=both semantics explicitly: either make it journey-level only and call F002 with the derived concrete SurfaceFamily for each surface_class, or define and test the exact both x surface_class matrix.

findings.description: The qualitative claim_kind cell is not coherent across the closed surface_class enum. F002 states qualitative returns rubric|human_signoff, but agent-family surfaces with consumer=agent are otherwise valid tuples and would be asked to satisfy a human-only evidence group.
findings.recommendation: Pin qualitative requirements per family or reject qualitative for agent-family surfaces with a tested explicit error.

findings.description: F002 contains conflicting aggregation language: it says aggregation granularity is surface_class and same-class tokens form one group, but also says each declared surface forms its own requirement set and groups are not deduplicated across surfaces. This leaves ios+android and other same-class token cases ambiguous.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite the aggregation rule around one unit only, preferably surface_class as stated by D065, and add an explicit ios+android same-class aggregation test.

findings.description: F001 requires a documented evidence_class to existing EvidenceRef.type table, but the proposed feature does not pin the table cells for the full closed evidence_class enum. F003 only constrains the agent subset, leaving human, mutation, and structured classes open to inconsistent implementation choices.
findings.recommendation: Pin the complete evidence_class -> allowed EvidenceRef.type mapping in F001 and assert every enum member is covered exactly as intended.

findings.description: F001 says consumer is required for journeys asserting a consumer-facing outcome, but the plan does not define the structural signal used to determine that a journey is consumer-facing. Without that discriminator, omission rejection can drift between always-required and heuristically-required behavior.
findings.recommendation: Define the validator trigger explicitly, such as all objective_contract.user_journeys under this gate require consumer, or add a concrete consumer_facing boolean and test both branches.
